name: Bourbeuse River — Mint Spring Access to Chouteau Claim Access
blurb: Bourbeuse River in Missouri: sections between public Missouri Department of Conservation accesses.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

sections.notes: Put-in Mint Spring Access: exact agency access pin. Take-out Tea Access: approximate area only. Missouri law: no glass beverage containers on canoes, kayaks or tubes; keep food and drink in a sealed non-glass cooler; carry a closable trash bag affixed to the boat; children under 7 wear life jackets. Banks and gravel bars beside private land may be private — use public accesses. Mileage: preliminary, measured along USGS river geometry (no agency mileage found).

putInAccess.sourceName: MDC Discover Nature — Boat Ramp features, OBJECTID 156
putInAccess.note: MDC Discover Nature — Boat Ramp features, OBJECTID 156 (Boat ramp (MDC)) is the managing agency's own access feature, 38 m from the USGS NHD High Resolution flowline of the Bourbeuse River. Imagery check 2026-10-30: Pin at a parking area, path head or ramp head within roughly 40-60 m of the water with a visible route to the bank. Public access: Missouri Department of Conservation — Mint Spring Access (area page).

takeOutAccess.sourceName: Missouri Department of Conservation — Tea Access (area page)
takeOutAccess.note: Public river access is documented by Missouri Department of Conservation — Tea Access (area page). The coordinate is MDC Conservation Area centroids (Discover Nature atlas) — area centroid; approximate area, not the exact launch. Why not exact: the MDC record is a conservation-area centroid, not a launch feature.
takeOutAccess.directions: From Owensville take Highway 19 south 2 miles, then Route V east 5 miles, and Route T south 4 miles to Tea Road.
